items.description: Analyze repository structure, tooling capabilities, and agent hierarchy
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/repo_analysis.json` documenting: (1) all modules in `.archivara/` and `.opencode/` with their purposes, (2) the ConceptEvolve pipeline (evolve/probe/reframe/walk) and how sub-agents are dispatched, (3) the Semantic Scholar integration and BibTeX export capability, (4) the agent hierarchy (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker) and their tool permissions, (5) the `results/concept_evolve/tree/` folder convention for concept cards. Must be valid JSON with at least 5 top-level sections.

items.description: DEFLATE format deep-dive: map the sequential dependency chain that limits decompression throughput
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/001_deflate_format_analysis/concept.json` containing: (1) formal description of DEFLATE's three block types (uncompressed, fixed Huffman, dynamic Huffman) with bit-level layout, (2) diagram of the decode loop's sequential dependency chain (peek bits -> table lookup -> consume variable bits -> output literal or execute copy -> repeat), (3) quantified critical-path latency per symbol on modern x86 (Zen4) and ARM (Apple M4) citing cycle counts from Agner Fog's instruction tables or vendor optimization manuals, (4) identification of the three fundamental serialization barriers: Huffman variable-length codes preventing bit-parallel decode, LZ77 back-reference data dependency on output history, and bit-stream position tracking requiring serial consumption. Must cite at least 3 technical sources (RFC 1951, Agner Fog tables, one microarchitecture manual).

items.description: Comprehensive literature review via web search: DEFLATE decompression optimization papers, codebases, and techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Using websearch and webfetch tools, locate and summarize at least 15 relevant sources covering: (a) optimized single-core CPU implementations (zlib-ng, libdeflate, ISA-L, zlib-rs, zlib-cloudflare, zlib-chromium, WUFFS, fdeflate, dougallj's experimental zlib fork), (b) parallel/multi-core decompression approaches (pugz, rapidgzip, pigz, pzstd analogs), (c) GPU-accelerated approaches (nvCOMP/GDeflate, CUHD massively parallel Huffman decoding), (d) hardware accelerators (Intel QAT, FPGA DEFLATE engines), (e) foundational bit-IO and entropy coding optimization (Fabian Giesen's 'Reading bits in far too many ways' series, Yann Collet's Huff0/FSE, ANS coding comparisons). Produce `results/concept_evolve/literature_review.json` with an array of objects each containing: title, authors, year, venue_or_url, category (one of: cpu_optimized, parallel, gpu, hardware, foundational), key_insight (1-2 sentences), reported_throughput_if_any, and relevance_score (1-10). Must include at least 3 sources per category.
items.notes: Requires web search and web fetch for real-time information gathering

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted references
items.acceptance_criteria: Create `sources.bib` in the repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 relevant papers and technical references. Must include entries for: (1) RFC 1951 - Deutsch 1996 DEFLATE specification, (2) pugz - Kerbiriou & Chikhi 2019/2020 parallel gzip decompression, (3) rapidgzip - Knespel & Brunst 2023 parallel random-access gzip, (4) Weissenberger & Schmidt 2018 massively parallel Huffman decoding on GPUs, (5) at least one Intel ISA-L reference, (6) at least one FPGA DEFLATE implementation paper, (7) libdeflate technical documentation or associated benchmarks, (8) Fabian Giesen's bit-reading optimization work, and (9) at least 2 additional sources. Each entry must have title, author, year, and either doi or url. Use the semantic_scholar bibtex command where paper IDs are available.
items.notes: Use semantic_scholar bibtex export for entries where paper IDs are known

items.description: ConceptEvolve exploration: generate cross-domain concept cards for DEFLATE speedup strategies
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute ConceptEvolve `evolve` with topic 'Making DEFLATE decompression 2-5x faster than any existing implementation by exploiting speculative execution, SIMD parallelism, and novel algorithmic decomposition'. Verify that `results/concept_evolve/tree/` contains at least 8 concept folders, each with `concept.json` and `README.md`. Verify `results/concept_evolve/concept_cards.json` exists with at least 8 cards spanning at least 3 distinct domains. Verify `results/concept_evolve/semantic_bridge.json` has nodes and edges forming a connected graph. Verify `results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json` and `results/concept_evolve/tree/adjacency.json` exist. Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to cross-reference the concept cards against the literature review (item_003) and annotate each card with supporting citations from sources.bib.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner for citation cross-referencing against concept cards

items.description: Competitive landscape analysis: benchmark claims and throughput comparison matrix across all known DEFLATE implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/002_competitive_landscape/concept.json` containing a structured comparison matrix of all known DEFLATE decompression implementations with columns: name, language, single_core_throughput_MBps (on Silesia corpus or equivalent standard benchmark), parallelism_model (none/block-level/stream-level), SIMD_usage (none/SSE4/AVX2/NEON/SVE), streaming_api (yes/no), format_compatibility (deflate-only/gzip/zip/all), license, and notable_technique. Must include at least 12 implementations. Include a 'gap_analysis' field identifying the specific performance gaps: stock zlib (~250 MB/s), best optimized zlib-compatible (~450 MB/s zlib-ng), best single-core non-streaming (~1100 MB/s libdeflate), and best parallel (~10+ GB/s rapidgzip with many cores). All throughput numbers must cite specific benchmark sources from the literature review. Define explicit 2x and 5x target thresholds relative to the best single-core implementation.
items.notes: Depends on item_003 for benchmark citations

items.description: Establish benchmarking infrastructure, corpus selection, and measurement methodology
items.acceptance_criteria: Create `results/concept_evolve/tree/003_benchmark_infra/concept.json` specifying: (1) benchmark corpus with rationale -- must include Silesia corpus (all 12 files), Canterbury corpus, at least one large gzip file >1GB (e.g., enwiki dump), a PNG test suite with varied image types, and synthetic worst-case inputs (maximum-distance references, all-literals, pathological Huffman distributions), (2) measurement methodology: wall-clock time via high-resolution timer, CPU cycles via rdtsc/perf_event, throughput as MB/s of decompressed output, cache miss rates (L1d, L2, LLC) via perf stat, branch misprediction rate, IPC (instructions per cycle), (3) statistical rigor: minimum 30 runs per measurement, report median and 95th percentile, first 5 runs excluded as warmup, Wilcoxon signed-rank test for pairwise comparisons at p<0.05, (4) hardware specification template requiring: CPU model + stepping, base/boost frequency, L1/L2/L3 cache sizes, memory bandwidth, compiler + flags. Produce a `benchmarks/README.md` specification describing the planned benchmark harness.
items.notes: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer subagent to verify the benchmark design covers all concept-card scenarios from item_005

items.description: Profile zlib reference implementation to identify hotspot functions and microarchitectural bottlenecks
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/004_zlib_profiling/concept.json` with a detailed profile of zlib 1.3.x inflate path showing: (1) percentage of execution time in each major function (inflate(), inflate_fast(), inflate_table(), updatewindow(), adler32()), (2) branch misprediction hotspots with specific source locations (file:line) in inflate_fast's main decode loop, (3) cache behavior analysis: Huffman table sizes vs. L1d capacity, sliding window access pattern vs. L2, (4) IPC measurement showing actual IPC (~1.2-1.5 expected) vs. theoretical pipeline width (4-6 on Zen4/M4), (5) quantified overhead of zlib's streaming API vs. one-shot decompression (inflate() call overhead, state save/restore cost), (6) comparison of inflate_fast's chunked approach vs. the main inflate() fallback. Must identify the top 3 bottlenecks by cycle contribution. Reference prior work from the literature review (item_003) to contextualize findings.
items.notes: Depends on item_007 for measurement methodology

items.description: Baseline throughput measurements across reference implementations on standardized corpus
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/005_baseline_measurements/concept.json` with measured decompression throughput (MB/s of decompressed output) for at least 6 implementations: zlib (stock), zlib-ng, libdeflate, Intel ISA-L, one Rust implementation (zlib-rs or fdeflate), and one parallel implementation (rapidgzip or pugz). Each measurement must include: mean, median, stddev, p95 throughput on each Silesia corpus file and a weighted aggregate. Results must be presented as a comparison table and must validate or contradict throughput claims from the literature review (item_003), with explicit notes on discrepancies. Include a 'target_throughput' field defining specific 2x and 5x targets: e.g., if libdeflate measures 1050 MB/s, 2x = 2100 MB/s and 5x = 5250 MB/s single-core, or multi-core equivalents.
items.notes: Depends on item_007 (benchmark infrastructure) and item_003 (literature throughput claims)

items.description: Micro-benchmark the four critical bottleneck stages of DEFLATE decompression independently
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/006_microbenchmarks/concept.json` with isolated micro-benchmarks for: (1) Huffman table construction time -- dynamic blocks of varying code-length alphabet sizes (19-entry, 286-entry, 30-entry distance), measuring cycles per table build, (2) Huffman symbol decode throughput -- symbols per second for various code-length distributions (uniform, Zipfian, degenerate), measuring the ~6-7 cycle critical path per symbol, (3) LZ77 copy throughput -- varying distances (1, 4, 32, 1024, 32768) and lengths (3, 10, 64, 258), with and without SIMD memcpy/memmove, measuring cycles per output byte, (4) bit-buffer refill overhead -- conditional refill (branch on bits remaining) vs. unconditional 64-bit refill with shift, measuring branch misprediction penalty. Each micro-benchmark must report cycles per operation and identify which stage dominates for: typical text (Silesia), binary executables, PNG-style filtered data, and adversarial inputs. Delegate to a concept-tree-explorer subagent to map bottleneck measurements to concept cards from item_005 and identify which concepts address which bottlenecks.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer to map bottleneck-to-concept connections

items.description: Roofline model: derive theoretical throughput ceilings for single-core and multi-core DEFLATE decompression
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/007_roofline_model/concept.json` containing: (1) a roofline analysis relating decompression throughput to operational intensity (operations per byte of output) and memory bandwidth, (2) theoretical single-core throughput ceiling derived from: CPU frequency x IPC limit / critical-path-cycles-per-symbol / compression-ratio, with concrete numbers for Zen4 @ 5.0 GHz and Apple M4 @ 4.4 GHz, (3) theoretical multi-core throughput ceiling accounting for: memory bandwidth saturation point (at what core count does DDR5/LPDDR5 bandwidth become the bottleneck?), output write bandwidth, and inter-core synchronization overhead for block-boundary communication, (4) identification of which regime each optimization approach operates in: compute-bound (improving cycles/symbol), memory-bound (improving parallelism), or latency-bound (improving critical-path depth), (5) specific numerical targets: what cycles/symbol and IPC are needed to achieve 2x over libdeflate (~1100 MB/s) single-core, and what core-count/efficiency is needed for 5x. Must reference empirical micro-benchmark results from item_010.
items.notes: Depends on item_010 for empirical cycle counts per operation

items.description: Novel approach 1: Speculative multi-symbol Huffman decode with pre-computed conditional tables
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/008_speculative_multisymbol/concept.json` with: (1) detailed algorithm design for speculatively decoding 2-4 Huffman symbols per iteration from a single 64-bit bit-buffer by pre-computing conditional decode tables (entry key = packed bit window, value = {symbol_1, len_1, symbol_2, len_2, total_bits}), (2) analysis of the table size explosion: for max code length 15, a 2-symbol table needs 2^30 entries (impractical) -- describe the tiered approach (short-code fast table for codes <= 9 bits, then standard fallback) and quantify the practical table sizes for 2-symbol decode with root table of 9+9=18 bits (~1MB, fits L2), (3) rollback mechanism when the second symbol decode is invalid (crosses block boundary or hits end-of-block), (4) expected speedup calculation: reducing from ~6.5 cycles/symbol to ~4 cycles/two-symbols = ~3.25 cycles/symbol effective, validated against roofline from item_011, (5) comparison to: Fabian Giesen's interleaved multi-stream approach (requires format change), Oodle's 3-stream interleaving (proprietary, format change), and ISA-L's double-symbol decode (closest prior art). Must cite at least 3 entries from sources.bib.
items.notes: Depends on item_011 (roofline model) for speedup estimation framework

items.description: Novel approach 2: Hybrid parallel decompression combining speculative block-finding with optimized per-block decode
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/009_hybrid_parallel/concept.json` with: (1) algorithm combining rapidgzip-style speculative DEFLATE block boundary detection (scanning for valid dynamic Huffman headers) with libdeflate-quality per-block single-core decompression, (2) design for a work-stealing thread pool scheduler: producer thread scans for block boundaries and enqueues block descriptors (compressed_offset, decompressed_offset_estimate); consumer threads decompresses blocks; coordinator thread validates decompressed offsets match and patches up cross-block LZ77 references, (3) analysis of false-positive rate for speculative block finding (quantified from pugz/rapidgzip published results: ~0.1-1% false starts) and its throughput impact, (4) strategy for the worst case: single-block files where block-level parallelism is impossible -- fall back to single-core optimized decode from approach 1, (5) design for optional pre-computed block index (stored as sidecar file or appended metadata) that eliminates speculation overhead for repeated decompression. Must compare quantitatively against rapidgzip's published 10 GB/s on 12 cores. Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to mine the citation graph of Knespel & Brunst 2023 (rapidgzip) for additional parallel decompression techniques not yet covered.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner on rapidgzip citation graph for additional parallel techniques

items.description: Novel approach 3: SIMD-accelerated branchless decode loop for modern x86-64 and AArch64 microarchitectures
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/010_simd_branchless_decode/concept.json` with: (1) design for a branchless inner decode loop eliminating the branch misprediction bottleneck: use conditional moves (CMOV) or predicated operations instead of branches for literal-vs-match classification, unconditional 64-bit bit-buffer refill every iteration (paying ~1 wasted cycle to avoid the conditional-refill branch misprediction), (2) SIMD-accelerated multi-byte LZ77 copy: using 16-byte SIMD loads/stores (SSE2/NEON) for all copy operations, handling the overlapping-copy case (distance < length) via repeated 16-byte overlapping copies with distance-based shuffle masks, (3) design for a 'short-code literal burst' fast path: detect when the next N symbols are all short-code (<= 8-bit) literals and decode them 4-8 at a time using a packed lookup table, extending dougallj's technique, (4) cycle count comparison: branchless SIMD path vs. scalar branchy path on Zen4 (expected: eliminate ~2 cycles/symbol from branch mispredictions) and Apple M4 (expected: smaller gain due to better branch predictor), (5) fallback strategy for when fast path is not applicable (long codes, many back-references) -- seamless transition to scalar path without pipeline flush. Must cite dougallj's work and ISA-L's inflate approach in sources.bib.

items.description: Novel approach 4: Two-pass decode with lightweight bit-boundary preprocessing for intra-block parallelism
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/011_bitstream_preprocessing/concept.json` with: (1) design for a two-pass algorithm: Pass 1 scans the bitstream using the Huffman table to record symbol boundaries (bit offsets and symbol types: literal/length/distance) into a compact index without writing output; Pass 2 uses the index to decode symbols and execute LZ77 copies, potentially partitioned across multiple threads, (2) cost analysis of Pass 1: since it must do full Huffman decode to find bit boundaries (prefix codes are not self-synchronizing mid-stream), Pass 1 costs approximately the same as full decode minus the copy work -- quantify the net benefit (only worthwhile if copy work is >30% of total), (3) alternative design: exploit the fact that dynamic Huffman blocks repeat the same code table -- if two threads start decoding from estimated mid-block positions, one will eventually synchronize with the correct bitstream (similar to pugz's approach but at sub-block granularity), (4) comparison to GDeflate's modified format with bit-swizzled blocks (our approach preserves standard DEFLATE format), (5) break-even analysis: for what block sizes and compression ratios does two-pass become faster than single-pass? Must quantify preprocessing overhead vs. parallelism benefit.

items.description: Novel approach 5: Adaptive multi-kernel decode with runtime workload classification
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/012_adaptive_decode/concept.json` with: (1) design for a decoder that samples the first K symbols (K=64-256) of each dynamic Huffman block and selects from specialized decode kernels: (a) literal-dominated kernel (>80% literals): uses wide lookup table and burst decode, (b) short-code kernel (90%+ codes <= 9 bits): uses 9-bit root table only, no secondary table lookups, (c) copy-heavy kernel (>40% back-references): uses SIMD copy with prefetch of output history, (d) general kernel: full decode path for complex distributions, (e) parallel kernel: for blocks exceeding size threshold, applies approach from item_015, (2) the sampling heuristics: build code-length histogram during table construction (already available), compute literal/match ratio from first K symbols, measure average code length, (3) expected overhead: ~50-100 cycles for kernel selection vs. potential savings of 0.5-2 cycles/symbol over the general path, (4) comparison to WUFFS's compile-time specialization (static, cannot adapt to input) and ISA-L's runtime CPU feature dispatch (adapts to hardware, not workload). Must connect to at least 2 concept cards from the ConceptEvolve tree (item_005) via explicit cross-references.

items.description: Concept-tree synthesis: rank concept paths by estimated impact, identify blind spots, and produce prioritized implementation roadmap
items.acceptance_criteria: Run ConceptEvolve `walk` on the concept tree from item_005 and produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/013_synthesis/concept.json` containing: (1) the top 5 highest-impact concept paths ranked by estimated throughput improvement (grounded in roofline analysis from item_011), (2) for each path: a concrete implementation plan with estimated effort in person-days, required hardware/software dependencies, and risk assessment (low/medium/high), (3) a dependency graph showing which novel approaches (items 012-016) map to which concept cards and which bottleneck stages (from item_010), (4) identification of at least 2 'blind spot' areas: optimization directions where the concept tree has no coverage but the literature review (item_003) or citation graph mining suggests real opportunity, (5) a prioritized 4-week roadmap ordering approaches by expected throughput-gain-per-effort-day. Delegate to a concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse the full tree and identify missing cross-domain connections and unexplored adjacencies.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for full tree traversal, gap analysis, and adjacency exploration

items.description: Experiment 1: Implement and benchmark speculative multi-symbol Huffman decode
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/014_exp_speculative/concept.json` with: (1) working implementation in C (with intrinsics) or Rust of the speculative 2-symbol Huffman decode from item_012, integrated into a complete DEFLATE decompressor, (2) benchmark results on all 12 Silesia corpus files comparing against libdeflate and ISA-L baselines from item_009, (3) measurements of: throughput (MB/s), cycles per output byte, cycles per symbol, speculation success rate (% of iterations where both symbols decoded correctly without rollback), table memory usage in bytes, (4) per-file analysis: which Silesia files benefit most (expected: text-heavy with short codes) vs. least (expected: already-compressed data with uniform code distributions), (5) statistical significance: Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p<0.05 for all pairwise comparisons with baselines. Results must validate or invalidate the roofline predictions from item_011.

items.description: Experiment 2: Implement and benchmark hybrid parallel decompression across core counts
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/015_exp_parallel/concept.json` with: (1) working implementation of the hybrid parallel decompressor from item_013 supporting configurable thread counts (1-N), (2) strong scaling analysis: throughput vs. core count (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 cores/threads) on at least 4 files of different sizes (1MB, 10MB, 100MB, 1GB compressed), (3) head-to-head comparison against rapidgzip on the same files and hardware, reporting both throughput and parallel efficiency (speedup / core_count), (4) identification of the scaling bottleneck: is it memory bandwidth, block-finding false positives, cross-block LZ77 dependencies, or thread synchronization? Quantify with roofline overlay, (5) weak scaling analysis: does throughput per core remain constant as file size increases? items.description: Experiment 3: Implement and benchmark SIMD branchless decode loop on x86-64 and AArch64
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/016_exp_simd/concept.json` with: (1) working implementation of the branchless SIMD decode loop from item_014 with both AVX2 (x86-64) and NEON (AArch64) code paths, (2) benchmark results on full Silesia corpus comparing against: libdeflate's scalar inflate, ISA-L's SIMD-accelerated inflate, and the speculative multi-symbol decode from item_018, (3) microarchitectural measurements via perf counters: branch misprediction rate reduction (expected: 3-5% -> <1%), IPC improvement (expected: 1.3 -> 1.8+), cycles-per-symbol reduction, (4) fast-path hit rate analysis: what percentage of decode iterations use the short-code literal burst path vs. falling back to scalar, broken down by file type, (5) cross-platform comparison: does the branchless approach help more on Zen4 (weaker branch predictor, wider pipeline) or Apple M4 (stronger branch predictor)? Quantify the difference.

items.description: Experiment 4: Integrate all techniques into combined decoder and evaluate interaction effects
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/017_exp_combined/concept.json` with: (1) implementation combining the best-performing techniques from experiments 1-3 into a single adaptive decoder (using the kernel selection from item_016), (2) full benchmark against ALL baselines from item_009 on the complete Silesia corpus plus PNG, git-pack, and >1GB gzip inputs, (3) interaction analysis: do the techniques compose multiplicatively (best case), additively, or sub-additively (interference)? Specifically: does speculative multi-symbol decode conflict with branchless SIMD (both modify the inner loop), and does parallel decomposition stack on top of per-core optimizations? (4) final single-core throughput with confidence intervals -- does it achieve 2x over libdeflate? (5) final multi-core throughput at 4 and 8 cores -- does it achieve 5x over stock zlib? Present results in a summary table with columns: implementation, 1-core MB/s, 4-core MB/s, 8-core MB/s, speedup-vs-zlib, speedup-vs-libdeflate. Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to search for any 2024-2026 publications that may have attempted similar technique combinations.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner for recent (2024-2026) related work. Depends on items 018-020, 016

items.description: Ablation study: quantify individual contribution of each optimization technique
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/018_ablation/concept.json` with: (1) systematic ablation study removing one optimization at a time from the combined decoder (item_021) and measuring throughput impact on 3 representative Silesia files (text: dickens, binary: x-ray, mixed: mr), (2) a waterfall/stacked contribution chart specification showing the additive (or sub-additive) contribution of: branchless decode, SIMD copy, speculative multi-symbol, unconditional refill, adaptive kernel selection, parallel decomposition, (3) interaction matrix: for each pair of optimizations, does enabling both give more or less than the sum of individual gains? (4) identification of the single most impactful optimization and the point of diminishing returns, (5) comparison of ablation results against the theoretical predictions from the roofline model (item_011): which predictions were accurate, which overestimated, and what explains the discrepancies (e.g., cache effects not modeled, branch predictor learning).

items.description: Correctness verification, edge-case testing, and adversarial input robustness evaluation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/019_adversarial/concept.json` with: (1) correctness verification: byte-for-byte output match against zlib on the entire Silesia corpus, Canterbury corpus, and a PNG test suite (at least 50 images), (2) DEFLATE conformance: pass all test vectors from the zlib test suite and Mark Adler's infcover test, (3) adversarial input performance: throughput on -- maximum 15-bit Huffman codes, blocks with only back-references (distance=1 RLE), blocks with only literals, near-maximum-size blocks (64KB uncompressed), minimum-size blocks (3-byte empty stored block), deeply nested zip/gzip containers, (4) performance ratio: does the novel decoder degrade more gracefully or less gracefully than libdeflate on adversarial inputs? Compute worst-case-to-best-case throughput ratio for each implementation, (5) memory safety: no buffer overflows or undefined behavior under any valid DEFLATE stream -- verified by at least 2 hours of coverage-guided fuzzing (AFL++ or libFuzzer) with no crashes and >80% edge coverage of the decode loop.

items.description: Future work roadmap: open problems, technology transfer opportunities, and format evolution analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/022_future_work/concept.json` with: (1) at least 5 concrete open problems with estimated difficulty (easy/medium/hard) and potential impact (low/medium/high): including intra-block parallelism without two-pass overhead, hardware-software co-design for next-gen DEFLATE accelerators, applying techniques to Brotli/Zstd decompression, GPU kernel design for standard DEFLATE (not GDeflate), and streaming API design that preserves optimization opportunities, (2) for each open problem: suggested approach, estimated person-months of effort, and at least one relevant citation from sources.bib, (3) 'technology transfer' section: which findings are immediately deployable as drop-in replacements in -- zlib-compatible libraries, nginx/Apache gzip decompression, PNG decoders (libpng, stb_image), Git pack-file decompression (libgit2), and browser content-encoding handlers, (4) format evolution analysis: should the community invest in DEFLATE optimization or migrate to Zstd/Brotli? Argue both sides citing ecosystem lock-in (billions of existing ZIP/gzip/PNG files), switching costs, and diminishing returns on DEFLATE optimization, (5) reference at least 3 concept cards from the tree that were identified as high-potential but not fully explored, with specific suggestions for follow-up research.
